name: Homer City Energy Campus
summary: Redevelopment of the retired Homer City coal-fired generating station in Indiana County, Pennsylvania, into a gas-fired power and data center campus of more than 3,200 acres. Seven GE Vernova 7HA.02 turbines are planned to deliver up to 4.4 GW for multiple large data center customers, with some power also supplied to the local grid. The developer projects more than 10 billion US dollars for power infrastructure and site readiness, with data centers adding more. Pennsylvania regulators issued an air permit in November 2025; by September 2026 more than 1,800 workers were on site, with power production targeted for 2027. No data center tenant has been named.

location.note: Coordinates of the former Homer City Generating Station from Wikipedia (s6), which places it in Center Township near the borough of Homer City; the campus is built on the former station site, which covers a large area, so the point is approximate.

power_sources.description: Seven GE Vernova 7HA.02 hydrogen-enabled gas turbines on site, burning Marcellus Shale gas; EQT is reported as the gas supplier.
The site keeps the former plant's connections to PJM and NYISO, and the campus is expected to supply some power to the local grid.
